Meet the colleagues

Two colleagues are talking

Amina and Sara work in the same office in a Gulf city, and they are getting to know each other.

What do you think they are talking about? Choose the ideas you like, or just think about it. There is no right or wrong answer.

They talk about experiences: places they have been to, and things they have not done yet.

The conversation

Hear what they say

Amina is a new colleague. She asks Sara a question about life in the Gulf.

A · Amina, new colleague

Have you ever been to the desert?

B · Sara, colleague

No, I haven’t. Not yet.

A · Amina, new colleague

Would you like to go?

B · Sara, colleague

Yes, I’d like to.

Amina’s photos

Look through the windows

Sara looks at Amina’s photos and asks about them. Open the windows you like, in any order.

Choose a window above. Then Sara and Amina will talk about the photo.

Sara, colleague

Have you ever been to the desert?

Amina, new colleague

Yes, I have. I went last winter.

Sara, colleague

Have you ever been to the souk?

Amina, new colleague

Yes, once. It was interesting.

Sara, colleague

Have you ever driven in the desert?

Amina, new colleague

No, I haven’t. Not yet, but I’d like to.

Your day

Where could you say this?

Think about your own day. Where could you ask “Have you ever…?” Choose a place, or imagine your own situation.

You discovered useful language for this situation.

  • Have you ever…?
  • been to
  • No, I haven’t.
  • Not yet.
